thread.forceMemory.title: Continue despite the lack of memory?
thread.forceMemory.description: The check estimated that there is not enough free memory to load this model. macOS can compress or unload other applications to make room, but if memory really runs out, the machine may slow down a lot or freeze. The memory protection stays on and stops the model if the pressure becomes critical. Save your work before going on.
thread.footer.sameSeeds: Run again with the same seeds
thread.footer.sameSeeds.hint: Runs again with exactly the same seeds: gives the same result. Useful after changing a setting, to judge its effect alone.
thread.footer.vary.body: Runs the same prompt again with new random seeds: each try gives a different result. Previous images are kept.
thread.footer.vary.title: New variants (random seeds)
thread.help.count_images.body: How many variants to generate for this prompt, each with its own seed. They are computed one after the other: 4 images take about 4 times as long as one.
thread.help.count_images.title: Number of images
thread.help.count_takes.body: How many readings to generate for the same text, each with a different seed: intonation and rhythm vary from one take to the next. They are computed one after the other.
thread.help.count_takes.tip: make 2 or 3 takes, then keep the best one: the same voice never says it quite the same way twice.
thread.help.count_takes.title: Number of takes
thread.help.fast_decode.body: Uses a small, light decoder (TAEHV) to turn the final result into frames. Decoding drops from several minutes to under a second, especially on a Mac. In return, fine details are slightly less sharp.
thread.help.fast_decode.tip: keep it on to explore; turn it off for the final render if you see crushed details.
thread.help.fast_decode.title: Fast decoding
thread.help.guidance.body: How closely the model must stick to your prompt. Low: freer and more natural, sometimes approximate. High: more faithful, but images that are too contrasted or "burnt" if overdone. At 1, guidance is off (which speeds things up, since the model computes one pass instead of two).
thread.help.guidance.tip: stay close to the default value; change it half a point at a time.
thread.help.guidance.title: Guidance (CFG)
thread.help.negative_prompt.body: What the result must avoid: "blur, text, extra fingers, watermark"... Describe flaws or elements, not sentences ("without X" works poorly in the main prompt).
thread.help.negative_prompt.tip: leave empty if all is well. On a model without guidance (1 = off), it has no effect.
thread.help.negative_prompt.title: Negative prompt
thread.help.seed.body: Number that sets the starting noise. Left empty, a random seed is drawn at each generation: each try gives a different result. Pinned, the same prompt with the same settings gives exactly the same result. "Vary" and "Redo" draw new seeds; the ↻ "same seeds" button reuses them.
thread.help.seed.tip: pin the seed of a result you like, then change only one setting at a time to see its effect.
thread.help.seed.title: Seed
thread.help.speed.body: Reading pace. 1 = natural speed; below it the voice slows down, above it speeds up. Extreme values (< 0.8 or > 1.25) can sound less natural.
thread.help.speed.title: Speaking speed
thread.help.steps.body: Number of computing passes that bring the result out of noise. More steps = more finesse and coherence, but a proportional computing time; beyond a certain point the gain becomes invisible.
thread.help.steps.tip: keep the default value; lower it for a quick draft. A "distilled" or "turbo" model needs only 4 to 9 steps.
thread.help.steps.title: Steps
thread.help.strength.body: Balance between the starting image and your prompt when starting from an existing image: on one side the result stays close to the original, on the other the model moves away from it to follow the text. The exact meaning depends on the model (see below).
thread.help.strength.tip: try 2 or 3 values with the same seed to find the right balance.
thread.help.strength.title: Influence
thread.help.strength_video.body: How much transformation is applied to the source video. Low: the result stays close to the original. High: the model follows your prompt more, at the cost of moving away from the video.
thread.help.strength_video.tip: 0.6 to 0.8 for a change of style; lower for a light touch-up.
thread.help.strength_video.title: Video influence
thread.help.temperature.body: How much chance goes into the intonation. Low: a steady, predictable voice. High: more expressive and varied, but less stable (hesitations, drifting accents).
thread.help.temperature.tip: 0.9 suits most texts; lower it for a long text to be read evenly.
thread.help.temperature.title: Variability
